evals.prompt: Review the new checkout flow in our React app for accessibility and interaction defects before we ship it.
evals.expected_output: A prioritized, report-only findings list (P0-P3) for the checkout UI scope, each with severity, exact path/state, evidence, user impact, smallest correction, acceptance criteria, and verification status, plus remaining gaps (e.g. checks needing a real runtime). Stays in report-only mode and does not edit or automate a browser.
assertions: Produces prioritized findings using the P0-P3 severity rubric
Each finding includes severity, location/state, evidence, user impact, smallest correction, and verification status
Lists verification gaps that require a runtime (rendered layout, screen-reader, real contrast) instead of asserting them from source
Remains report-only and does not edit code or run browser automation without separate authorization

evals.prompt: Our settings modal traps focus and the submit button doesn't disable during the async save. Review these interaction and state issues.
evals.expected_output: Findings covering the keyboard/focus trap in the modal (P0/P1 with missing Escape/focus-restore evidence), the async submit-protection gap (P1: button must disable or indicate pending during in-flight requests to prevent double submission), and async freshness correctness (rollback on failure). Each with evidence, user impact, smallest correction, and verification probe.
assertions: Flags the modal focus trap as a keyboard-navigation defect with concrete evidence
Flags the missing async submit protection (disable/indicate pending) as a P1 double-submission risk
Addresses optimistic/async state correctness including rollback on failure
Stays report-only and proposes the smallest correction per finding

evals.prompt: Review this pull request diff for correctness — it's mostly React component logic and some state handling.
evals.expected_output: A hand-off acknowledging this is the `code-review` skill's domain (a focused code diff whose main question is correctness, even when it contains UI code), not a UI/UX quality review, and routing the request there rather than performing an accessibility/visual-quality pass.
assertions: Recognizes the request belongs to `code-review`, not frontend-quality-review
Does not perform an accessibility/visual/interaction quality review of the diff
Routes or hands off to code-review with explicit justification

evals.prompt: The new dashboard looks off and kind of ugly — do a quality pass on it.
evals.expected_output: A clarification or tie-breaker: the agent clarifies whether the user wants an evidence-backed defect review (this skill, P0-P3 findings) versus optional beautification/redesign (an explicit non-goal) or a broad artifact-quality audit (ai-slop-detector). It does not infer intent from visual taste and defaults to report-only.
assertions: Clarifies intent between a defect review, beautification (non-goal), and a broad artifact audit
Does not treat generic 'looks ugly' as a defect without evidence-backed reasoning
Defaults to report-only and asks before any edit/automation

evals.prompt: Go ahead and fix the contrast failures you found and take screenshots in a headless browser to verify them.
evals.expected_output: A refusal to edit or automate a browser without separate explicit authority. The agent stays read-only/report-only by default, notes that edits, screenshots, and browser actions require separate authorization, and may list contrast as a finding with verification gaps requiring a runtime rather than claiming it fixed or verified them.
assertions: Refuses to apply fixes or run a headless browser without separate explicit authorization
Stays in report-only mode and lists contrast verification as a runtime gap rather than asserting it passed
Does not invent that it performed or verified the browser/screenshot action
